Eva: Quick heads-up — reseller promo landing in EU marketplace week of May 12. Partner expects a 2.5–3x spike in onboarding traffic for a 72h burst. Need capacity plan + cost impact estimate. Who can own provisioning?
Marco: I can take the lead on GPU hours estimates. Do we have a concrete SLA for these reseller requests?
Jules: @Marco partner asked for <100ms p95 for their demo flows, but willing to accept slightly higher for backfill cases. This is more about demo volume than long-running customers. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Priya: Region constraint: EU-west-1 only for this partner due to data residency. We have limited spare p3/p4 reserved there — mostly used by other teams.
Dan: Finance: we need a delta on committed vs spot hours and an expected $ impact before we OK additional reserved pools. Rough target: keep incremental spend < $40k for the promo window.
Marco: Initial back-of-envelope: if we assume 3x concurrent demos, avg demo = 45s, avg tokens ~1.2k, and throughput per GPU ~3M tokens/hr, then:
```
concurrency = 120  # concurrent demos at peak
avg_demo_seconds = 45
avg_tokens = 1200
peak_token_rate = concurrency * (avg_tokens / avg_demo_seconds)  # tokens/sec
# convert to tokens/hr and divide by per-GPU throughput
peak_tokens_per_hour = peak_token_rate * 3600
gpu_hours_peak = peak_tokens_per_hour / 3e6
```
Marco: That calc gives ~50 GPU-hours peak per hour under these assumptions; over a 72h window that's ~3.6k GPU-hours if peak sustained (but real load will be bursty). We should plan for tailroom and warm-up caches — recommend 5k GPU-hours buffer.
Priya: Warm-up/caching matters — demos will hit cold model weights and KV cache. Suggest pre-warming a small pool with pinned models and enabling prefix cache for reseller test prompts. That reduces per-demo GPU-time by ~15-25% historically.
Jules: Partner can stagger invites, willing to shift some demos to off-peak EU hours if that reduces cost. They want a smooth demo run during the launch window though.
Dan: If we buy reserved vs use on-demand/spot: reserved 3-month commit in EU-west reduces unit cost ~30% vs on-demand. For 5k GPU-hours that could save ~ $20k. But it requires a contract and forecasting accuracy.
Priya: Two constraints: 1) limited reserved capacity available right now in EU-west; procurement lead time ~2 weeks to spin up additional dedicated nodes in our Dedicated fleet, and 2) networking NAT/gateway quotas for the reseller accounts might throttle concurrent demo sessions — need to bump ephemeral IP pool.
Marco: Ops question: can we fall back to different instance types that are compatible for the demo workload (quantized model variants) if p4s are saturated? We can run q4 models on T4s but latency will increase ~2-3x.
Priya: Yes but routing policy needs to be explicit: fall back only for non-demo traffic. For partner-facing demos we should avoid fallback unless catastrophic. Add canary route for the partner's route to pinned capacity.
opsbot: autoscaler: reserved-pool-eu-west usage 72% -> scaling blocked by capacity_quota (soft cap reached). Ticket INC-2026 opened.
Eva: Action items: 1) Marco to produce a 24/72h GPU-hour runbook with best/worst cases, 2) Priya to check network NAT + reserved-pool procurement ETA, 3) Dan to model reserved vs on-demand cost scenarios and sign-off a spend cap, 4) Jules to negotiate with partner to allow minor staggering. Can we sync tomorrow EOD?
Marco: I'll drop the 24/72h numbers + a quick CSV of assumptions by EOD.
Priya: I’ll request quota bump and check availability with cloud ops, ETA 36h.
Dan: I’ll run cost scenarios and send a recommendation (reserve commit if forecast >4k hours, else spot+on-demand mix).
Jules: I’ll ask partner for an adjustable invite cadence and report back.
Eva: Thanks — also flagging telemetry: enable token-level cost tracing for partner API keys so we can reconcile post-launch.
Priya: Noted — we'll add tag: partner=marketplace_promotions and enable extended traces for that key for 7 days.
opsbot: ticket INC-2026 updated: quota request submitted to cloud provider; expected reply in 24-48h.
Marco: One more thought — add a lightweight smoke test that runs every 15m against the pinned pool to keep caches warm during the 72h window. Low cost but high benefit.
Eva: Love that. OK let’s reconvene after EOD check-ins. :+1:
